items.text: Colts HC Shane Steichen ruled out TE Tyler Warren (groin) for Sunday vs Vikings; also Sauce Gardner (calf) out. Warren missed practice week and prior game.
items.why: Groin injury, DNPs all week; coach confirmation.
items.implication: Colts TE committee (Mallory/Alie-Cox etc) or more WR targets to Downs/Allen; reduced red-zone/ dual-threat options.
items.opportunity: Josh Downs or other pass-catchers get bump; handcuff TEs elevated.

items.text: Bears TE Cole Kmet believed to have suffered a serious, likely season-ending knee injury after being carted off Thursday vs Patriots; undergoing tests with no finality yet. Coach Ben Johnson said it 'didn't look very good.'
items.why: Non-contact knee buckle on catch, carted off; sources confirm serious.
items.implication: Major TE void in CHI offense; elevated role for Loveland as primary pass-catching TE and more snaps/routes for Burden in reduced multi-TE sets.
items.opportunity: Loveland routes/targets spike; Burden YPRR juice from fewer 2/3-TE sets.

items.text: Rams WR Puka Nacua calf injury from Thursday practice believed minor/not significant after tests; status for Sunday vs Raiders still up in the air as game-time decision possible. Left practice early, listed limited.
items.why: Calf issue in practice; tests show more minor than significant per sources.
items.implication: If out or limited, heavy target concentration elsewhere or TE reliance (Higbee); with Adams already IR, Puka volume was already massive.
items.opportunity: If OUT, backup WRs/TEs surge; if ACTIVE full, 25-tgt pace continues post-Ferguson delay.

items.text: Bucs HC Todd Bowles: Baker Mayfield 'looks like he’s ready to go' and expected to start Sunday vs Panthers after thumb injury.
items.implication: Stabilizes TB offense for Evans/Godwin/Irving; full starter snaps.
items.opportunity: Bucky Irving and pass-catchers retain full volume.

items.text: Lamar Jackson out on field for Friday practice (limited prior days) after left ankle injury missing two games; encouraging sign for potential return vs Bengals. Continues limited participation trend.
items.why: Spotted practicing Friday after limited Wed/Thu; day-to-day but positive progression.
items.implication: If active, boosts BAL offense, Flowers/Andrews/Henry usage and overall pace; Huntley otherwise.
items.opportunity: Full starter snaps if cleared; reverse Huntley beneficiaries.

items.text: The more I watch Jaylen Warren, the more I love his game. Steelers have something special. Loves him as RB9 @ NO for big workload in friendly matchup.
items.why: Film/workload + matchup vs NO defense carved by RBs; consistent volume.
items.implication: Strong start/flex; RB1 upside in PPR/standard this week.

items.text: TreVeyon Henderson played just 21% of snaps over last three weeks. Not like this for the rookie RB.
items.why: Snap share data last 3 weeks shows limited role.
items.implication: Henderson not a reliable start/flex; Stevenson retains lead back work despite any competition.
items.opportunity: Low for Henderson; monitor if role expands.

items.text: Luther Burden only 68.8% routes this season but elite 2.56 YPRR. Kmet injury may reduce 2-/3-TE sets, giving Burden even more juice/routes.
items.why: Route rate + elite efficiency; Kmet absence opens sets.
items.implication: Burden fantasy upside rises ROS/week with expanded opportunity; Loveland primary TE.
items.opportunity: Higher route share, targets, YPRR leverage for Burden.

items.text: Saquon Barkley back for Week 7 vs DAL; 'in line' to play. Efficient in two full games prior; DAL soft vs RBs. Viewing as RB15 value on return.
items.why: Return confirmed in-line; prior efficiency + matchup.
items.implication: Startable RB2/flex immediately; full workload expected.
items.opportunity: High snap/carry share vs soft DAL run D.

items.text: Loves A.J. Brown @ CHI (WR10): back in real role, elite volume potential vs Bears defense good for yardage. Also 33% target share, 97% routes Week 6 despite drops; buying the bounce.
items.why: Usage (tgt share/routes) + matchup; 10 Facts buy signal post-drops.

items.text: Josh Jacobs allowed in team meetings, lifting, medical at facility (non-football). Backups MarShawn Lloyd (49th EPA/rush) and Kaleb Johnson (53rd) quite bad amid OL mess. Discussed long-term on ROS Top-150.
items.why: Facility access positive; poor EPA from backups supports Jacobs return value.
items.implication: Jacobs ROS outlook solid if cleared soon; handcuffs not threatening.
items.opportunity: Jacobs reclaims lead role; Lloyd/Johnson limited.

items.text: Loves DeVonta Smith vs DAL (WR11) for elite volume and Tucker Kraft @ DET (TE6) as Lions D gift to pass-catchers. Also Chuba Hubbard, Bucky Irving for big workloads/friendly matchups.
items.why: Volume + matchups (Bears/Lions Ds soft to pass; RB-friendly for Hubbard/Irving).

items.text: Hates Rome Odunze vs NE, Josh Downs @ MIN, Travis Kelce @ SEA due to nasty matchups and suboptimal roles/target shares. Also hates Josh Jacobs (workload post-layoff), Cam Skattebo (brutal spot).
items.why: Matchup difficulty + role/target issues; Jacobs layoff questions.
items.implication: Sit/fade these; look elsewhere for starts.
items.conflict: Levitan more positive on Jacobs long-term.

items.text: 10 Facts: Stroud 6th-best QB last 3 wks, top yards/att; Nix 5.4 aDOT (no WR viable); Jeanty inefficient (<3 YPC 4/5), Washington 33% snaps/nearly equal rushes Week 6—role growth possible. Also AJ Brown buy, Mayer viable w/ Bowers, drop Brian Thomas (6% tgt).
items.why: Usage stats (snaps, aDOT, YPC, tgt share, routes).
items.implication: Stroud QB1 upside; fade Nix WRs; monitor Jeanty/Washington split; Mayer stream; drop Thomas.
items.opportunity: Washington snap/rush share rising if Jeanty inefficient; Mayer 70%+ routes.
